calculus-chapter-09-review-2-concept-che: x²+y²≥0, and zero derivative can occur only at the single point(0,0).
calculus-chapter-09-review-3-true-false-: x+y cannot be factored into a function of x times a function of y on an open region.
calculus-chapter-09-review-6-true-false-: e^y is nonlinear in the dependent variable.
calculus-chapter-09-review-7-true-false-: Positive logistic initial value1 approaches carrying capacity5.
calculus-chapter-09-review-1: Sign analysis of y(y−2)(y−4) makes0 and4 unstable and2 stable. Outside[0,4], cubic growth prevents existence for arbitrarily large forward time; do not call it a finite long-time limit.
calculus-chapter-09-review-2: Separate y dy=x dx. The original RHS x/y is undefined at y=0; select signs and connected domains using each initial point.
calculus-chapter-09-review-3: At y′=0 the derivative y″=2x−2yy′=2x; this determines the extremum type away from the origin. Euler uses the old x,y at each step.
calculus-chapter-09-review-4: Separate y^−2dy=2x dx and impose y0=1; the maximal interval through0 is(−1,1).
calculus-chapter-09-review-7: The left side is d(e^(y²))/dx. Integrate2x+3sqrt(x); do not discard either sign or the real-domain requirement.
calculus-chapter-09-review-8: After division by x², integrating factor e^(1/x) turns the equation into(e^(1/x)y)′=2x.
calculus-chapter-09-review-10: Separation yields ln(1+e^y)=−ln(1+cosx)+C; initial data set the product(1+e^y)(1+cosx)=4.
calculus-chapter-09-review-12: Integrate e^−y dy=3x²dx to get e^−y=e^−1−x³; the logarithm argument must stay positive.
calculus-chapter-09-review-13: Original slope is y. Orthogonal slope−1/y integrates to y²/2=−x+C; at y=0 interpret the vertical tangent geometrically.
calculus-chapter-09-review-14: Eliminate k via k=lny/x. Orthogonal slope=−x/(ylny); integrate ylny dy=−x dx. At the common point(0,1) the original family has multiple slopes, so no unique orthogonal direction is defined there.
calculus-chapter-09-review-15: Logistic solution has A=(2000−100)/100=19; solve the odds ratio for the requested population.
calculus-chapter-09-review-16: These are forecasts from the historical exercise data, not present-day population estimates. Fit exponential relative growth from6.1→6.9, or logistic odds(K−P)/P with K20; time is years after2000.
calculus-chapter-09-review-17: The remaining growth L_inf−L decays exponentially; impose initial length L0.
calculus-chapter-09-review-18: Salt input=1kg/min; outflow=10L/min times A/100kg/L. Thus A′=1−A/10,A0=0,A=10(1−e^−t/10).
calculus-chapter-09-review-19: I=5000/(1+(121/4)e^−kt). At one week the odds are19/6, so e^k=363/38. I4000 requires odds1/4 and e^kt=121.
calculus-chapter-09-review-20: The relative-rate proportionality integrates to lnR=klnS+constant.
calculus-chapter-09-review-21: Separate(k+h)dh/h=−(R/V)dt for h>0; retain h0 as an equilibrium. Positive solutions approach0 without crossing it.
calculus-chapter-09-review-22: The nullclines are y200 and x25000. Signs change around the equilibrium; the undamped Lotka–Volterra first integral gives a closed positive orbit.
calculus-chapter-09-review-23: With x25000, insect zero growth requires0.4(1−0.125)−0.002y=0, hence y175. The source trajectory spirals inward to that equilibrium.
calculus-chapter-09-review-24: This is the exercise’s simplified energy-balance model:10,000W′=1600−850−15W. InitialW60 gives exponential approach to50; t is days.
